jobs.description:
Job Description

At BNY, our culture allows us to run our company better and enables employees’ growth and success. As a leading global financial services company at the heart of the global financial system, we influence nearly 20% of the world’s investible assets. Every day, our teams harness cutting-edge AI and breakthrough technologies to collaborate with clients, driving transformative solutions that redefine industries and uplift communities worldwide.

Recognized as a top destination for innovators, BNY is where bold ideas meet advanced technology and exceptional talent. Together, we power the future of finance – and this is what is all about. Join us and be part of something extraordinary.

We’re seeking a future team member for the role of Senior Vice President, ETF Product to join our ETF Services business. This role can be located in New York City, NY/Boston, MA/Lake Mary, FL/Los Angeles, CA.

Position Summary

Higher level of experience and expertise in product management. Responsible for strategic product planning, managing multiple product backlogs, and mentoring junior Product owners.

In this role, you’ll make an impact in the following ways:

Product Execution

Able to contribute meaningfully to specs for major features within the ETF platform
Able to negotiate the implementation of current work, make the right trade-off decisions to launch product in a high-quality manner
Know when to escalate to manager
Work with team to make recommendations that deliver maximum value to the ETF ecosystem as quickly as possible.
Can efficiently assess the quality and readiness of a feature

Customer Insights

Formulate the right business questions to be asked and how to track down data to inform decisions
Can use low fidelity tools to outline a design approach and then work with your team to translate into higher fidelity representation of the feature
Regular contact with users of product and use multiple sources to prioritize ETF roadmap decisions

Product Strategy

Leads product management and strategy for large and/or complex projects for the ETF Services business
Understands the economics behind and demonstrate business acumen for the ETF investment vehicle
Leverages market knowledge to integrate demands of the various regions and stay ahead of competitors

Primary Responsibilities

Develops ideas for new products, services, and technology to support the end-to-end workflow of an ETF
Independently manages the development, enhancement, and profitability and penetration of ETF-related products
Positions capabilities for specific client types, highlighting key benefits and competitive advantages
Engagement with Sales and Relationship Management in supporting business development opportunities
Performs demonstrations and develops user material for clients

To be successful in this role, we’re seeking the following:

Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent combination of education and experience is required. MBA or CFA preferred.
Minimum of 5 years of direct ETF Services, ETF Product, ETF Capital Markets, or ETF AP Desk experience required
Minimum of 10 years of overall financial services experience is strongly preferred

Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Royal Bank of Canada is seeking an experienced Director-level professional to serve as Product Owner for FX and Money Markets Operations. This strategic role leverages significant domain knowledge of FX markets, trading workflows, and post-trade processes to shape RBC's operations in this key business line. You will oversee the development and management of our client-facing FX platform, translate operational needs into technical solutions, and ensure regulatory and operational compliance. This position drives operational efficiency, automation, and settlement risk mitigation while collaborating with front-office stakeholders to ensure operational readiness for ongoing industry transformation and evolving regulatory environments. This is an exceptional opportunity to make a lasting impact on one of RBC's most critical business functions.

What will you do?

Drive a modern FX and Money Markets global operations platform and manage the product backlog; collaborate across teams to implement features supporting trade lifecycle, risk mitigation, and compliance
Develop and implement efficient processes aligned with industry best practices and regulatory requirements; design solutions optimizing FX and Money Markets processing across multiple venues and asset types
Establish and track key performance indicators and service level agreements for settlement volumes, cycle times, exception rates, and operational efficiency gains; conduct regular process reviews and root cause analysis of settlement failures
Assess emerging technologies (AI, blockchain, real-time settlement capabilities) for potential adoption and support platform enhancements, system migration, and regulatory audits
Collaborate with internal departments (front-office, middle-office risk, compliance) to streamline FX and Money Markets processes; serve as escalation point for complex problems and client inquiries
Build and manage relationships with external infrastructure providers (CLS Net, DTCC, counterparties); deliver monthly and ad-hoc reporting on settlement metrics, operational risks, and regulatory compliance
Stay updated on industry regulations and regulatory developments across all jurisdictions; ensure compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements related to settlements; manage regulatory examinations and audits
Serve as subject matter expert on FX and Money Markets operations processes; advise front-office, risk, compliance, and technology teams; lead strategic projects such as FX Modernization readiness and settlement infrastructure upgrades.

What do you need to succeed?

Must-have:

Minimum 10–15 years of progressive experience in capital markets operations, with substantive exposure to FX and Money Markets operations
Proven track record leading operational transformation initiatives, including process redesign and change management
Strong understanding of trade settlement, clearing mechanics, payments, regulatory frameworks (including post-trade regulatory regimes), and operational risk management across multiple jurisdictions
Demonstrated experience navigating technology transitions and managing operational readiness for significant market infrastructure changes
Exceptional leadership and communication skills with ability to collaborate effectively across large, diverse, matrixed teams; proven ability to translate complex operational matters for senior leadership and regulators.

Nice-to-have:

MBA or equivalent advanced degree in Finance, Business Administration, or related field
FINRA Series 99 certification
Prior experience in operational governance roles and exposure to regulatory examinations with demonstrated ability to manage remediation initiatives
Experience with operational resilience testing, business continuity planning in settlement environments, or leading strategy on major market infrastructure transitions
Familiarity with workflow automation, exception management systems, and emerging technologies in back-office operations

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program include competitive compensation and flexible benefits, such as 401(k) program with company-matching contributions, health, dental, vision, life, disability insurance, and paid-time off.
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities.
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact.
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.
Opportunities to do challenging work.
Opportunities to build close relationships with clients.

The expected salary range for this particular position is $180,000 - 250,000, depending on your experience, skills, and registration status, market conditions and business needs.

You have the potential to earn more through RBC’s discretionary variable compensation program which gives you an opportunity to increase your total compensation, provided the business meets its performance targets and you meet your individual goals.

Drives RBC’s high-performance culture
Enables collective achievement of our strategic goals
Generates sustainable shareholder returns and above market shareholder value

Job Description

We’re seeking a future team member for the role of Director, Product Design
to join our Fund and Investor Solutions team. This role is based in New York, NY.

In this role, you’ll make an impact in the following ways:

We are seeking a Senior Product Designer with experience working with, defining, and designing complex systems to bring creativity, strategic insight, and user-centered thinking to our team. This role requires an individual who excels in collaboration, design execution, and the ability to drive impactful user experiences.

The Ideal Candidate Will Bring the Following Expertise

Craft

User-Centered Design – Lead with a user-first approach, ensuring all design choices address user needs, behaviors, and insights from research. Drive a seamless and intuitive product experience by deeply understanding our users.
Journey Mapping – Map and analyze end-to-end user journeys across customers, operations, servicing teams and systems to identify pain points, key moments, and opportunities for improvement. Use journey maps to align teams on a shared vision of user needs, ensuring a cohesive and supportive experience at each stage.
Interaction and UI Design – Demonstrates mastery in designing complex web interfaces and workflows, creating products that are both highly functional and visually engaging. Skilled in developing intuitive layouts, navigation patterns, and interaction models for intricate systems. Thoughtfully uses animation and micro-interactions to guide users, making complex tasks more approachable and enhancing the overall product experience.
Proficiency in Design Tools – Possess advanced skills in tools such as Figma and Miro, to create high-fidelity wireframes, prototypes, and mockups that clearly communicate interaction models and UI specifications.

Systems thinking

Design System Knowledge – Experience with and contribute to a global design system that ensures visual consistency across interfaces. Develop workflow patterns and components that can then be reused by other teams.
Complex Systems Knowledge – Bring an understanding of the unique challenges of designing and maintaining complex systems, with an ability to distill intricate requirements into clear design solutions that facilitate user understanding and interaction.

Collaboration and Communication

Cross-Functional Collaboration – Work closely with product managers, engineers, and stakeholders to align design efforts with business goals, transforming complex requirements into clear, functional design solutions that respect technical constraints.
Effective Communication and Storytelling – Articulate design concepts and rationale to diverse stakeholders, making complex ideas accessible. Use storytelling to engage others in the product vision, fostering alignment and enthusiasm.

Mentorship and Leadership

Skilled in guiding junior designers, providing constructive feedback, and elevating team standards. Fosters a culture of continuous learning, innovation, and collaboration within the team.

A portfolio is required to be considered for this position

A portfolio is required and should demonstrate strong interaction design, systems thinking, and experience working in complex or ambiguous problem spaces. A Figma link with view access is acceptable.

Experience

Typically, a candidate at this level will have 12+ years of experience
designing digital products, including time spent on complex, enterprise, or regulated systems. Prior domain expertise is less important than demonstrated ability to learn new domains and apply strong design principles effectively.

Every day, our teams harness cutting-edge AI and breakthrough technologies to collaborate with clients, driving transformative solutions that redefine industries and uplift communities worldwide.

What if you could teach machines to make millions of delivery decisions — faster, smarter, and more efficiently than ever before? This isn't about incremental optimization. You will define and drive the product roadmap for AI/ML-powered solutions across the Sub Same Day delivery network — from supply chain planning and real-time capacity allocation to delivery and anomaly detection. You will serve as the connective tissue between data scientists, system development engineers, business intelligence engineers — ensuring technical feasibility, architectural soundness, and delivery velocity. About Sotheby's

Established in 1744, Sotheby’s promotes access and ownership of exceptional art and luxury objects through auctions, private sales and retail. Our deep expertise across 70 selling categories is supported by a leading technology platform and a global network of specialists spanning 40 countries. Selling categories include Contemporary Art, Modern and Impressionist Art, Old Masters, Chinese Works of Art, Jewelry, Watches, Wine and Spirits and Design, as well as collectible cars and real estate through RM Sotheby’s and Concierge. Sotheby’s Financial Services is a leading art lender and provides capital solutions for collectors around the world, having originated more than $12 billion in loans since its inception. Sotheby’s new global headquarters is now open at the iconic Breuer building at 945 Madison Avenue in New York City.

THE ROLE

The Senior Product Manager will support the VP of Product in owning, defining and driving the product roadmap for this new initiative, translating the business case into a shippable platform across a sequence of releases. This role will work closely with the VP of Product, engineering, design and the broader founding team to convert the product vision into precise requirements, sequenced releases and a defensible build-versus-buy point of view across the core platform. The ideal candidate is a motivated, detail-oriented operator who is comfortable running point on a complex, multi-workstream launch, translating ambiguity into a scoped roadmap, and partnering with a small, senior team to ship a premium product on a fixed date.

Responsibilities

Support the VP of Product in owning and maintaining the product roadmap across a sequence of major releases and the backlog beyond.
Run day-to-day agile ceremonies and stakeholder meetings across product, engineering, design and the wider operating team; track work in progress and unblock the delivery team.
Write precise, concise product requirements and specifications for core platform domains (identity, access, booking, payments, member services, CRM) in partnership with design and engineering.
Develop and maintain a point of view on build, buy or hybrid for each platform domain, and manage the resulting vendor and integration decisions behind a controlled interface layer.
Partner with membership, experience and service delivery leadership to ensure the platform supports the end-to-end member journey.
Own content-architecture and discovery requirements for member-facing editorial, ensuring it is structured for both member consumption and long-term platform needs.
Lead working sessions to make key decisions, remove obstacles and surface risks against a fixed launch timeline, escalating trade-offs to the VP of Product with clear recommendations.
Develop strong working partnerships with cross-functional leaders (Marketing, Finance, Legal) to keep the platform aligned to business objectives and launch dates.
Take on both tactical and strategic work depending on team needs, from Agile ceremony facilitation to stakeholder workshops and executive-ready materials.

Ideal Experience & Competencies

4–6 years of product management experience in e-commerce, membership, hospitality or technology platforms, ideally including at least one 0-to-1 or ground-up product launch.
Demonstrated interest in art, luxury or cultural institutions; an undergraduate degree in a technical field or a quantitative discipline is a strong plus.
Comfortable operating against a fixed, externally-driven launch date across multiple parallel workstreams (identity, booking, payments, content, CRM).
Organized, collaborative and flexible, able to work calmly and professionally under time-sensitive deadlines with a small, senior team.
Persuasive, with excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to write requirements a stranger could build from.
Logical problem solver with strong attention to detail and a data-first mindset, including familiarity with engagement scoring, retention or CRM-driven product work.
Experience evaluating build-versus-buy decisions and managing third-party vendors behind a defined interface layer.
Listens well to stakeholders and business owners while staying focused on delivering a high-quality, premium member experience.
Nimble with requirements gathering, analysis and documentation; and knows standard product management frameworks.
Functions well in an agile environment and has prior experience with cross-platform digital transformation projects.
Comfortable working on a confidential, pre-announcement initiative and maintaining discretion outside the immediate team.

jobs.description:
About DriveCentric

Founded in 2010 and headquartered in St. Louis, MO, with a distributed team across the US.
Backed by Summit Partners, with a mandate to grow, not to trim.
Trusted by 3,300+ dealerships across the US and Canada, from single-store independents to multi-billion-dollar dealer groups, plus adjacent retail such as RV, marine and powersports.
Launched the Service Engagement Hub in August 2026, the first engagement platform built for fixed operations, and ships autonomous AI agents (Sales, Prospect, Nurture, Service-to-Sales, Performance Management, Service) on a monthly cadence.
One of the first automotive software companies certified to ISO/IEC 42001 for AI management.
Runs DC20, a dealer-led peer community and event series that most vendors would call a user conference and our customers call a 20 Group.

Why this role exists now

Three things are true at once:
The portfolio is multiplying. We are moving from one product line to a platform spanning sales, service, data, F&I, payments and digital retail. Each department has a different buyer, a different competitor set and a different vocabulary. Nobody owns the messaging architecture that ties them together.
Product velocity is ahead of field readiness. Engineering and product are shipping at a pace the company has never operated at. Sales, account management, onboarding and support need enablement that is timely, credible and actually used, and we do not yet have the system to produce it.
The category is up for grabs. The market wants to put us in the CRM box. Our thesis is that AI agents change what "CRM" means, and the company that explains that best to a skeptical, relationship-driven buyer wins the next decade of auto retail software. That story needs an owner.

And one thing underneath all three: we are building an AI-native company, not a company with an AI product. Engineering ships with AI, our internal agents answer the field's questions, and every function is expected to automate its own work. Product marketing has to be built that way from day one, which is why the person who builds it matters so much.

You will report to the Chief Product & Business Officer and sit on the product leadership team alongside the VP Product, the AI Labs lead and the Head of Product Operations. Two product marketing managers will report to you on day one, with room to grow the team as the pillars scale.

What you will own

Positioning and narrative.
Build and maintain the messaging architecture for the platform and each of its pillars: the umbrella story, the per-department stories, and the proof that connects them. Lead the multi-year narrative evolution from CRM to AI Engagement Platform, and make it land with three very different audiences: the owner-operator of one store, the centralized buying group running 5 to 15 rooftops, and the enterprise group with a CFO in the room.

Launches
. Design and run our new product introduction system: launch tiers, the artifacts each tier gets, who does what, and how we measure whether the launch worked. Build it AI-first, so that a monthly agent cadence produces a full set of launch assets without a monthly scramble. Then run the big ones yourself. NADA Show (February, Orlando) is the industry's Dreamforce and our largest launch moment of the year; you will own the product marketing plan for it.

Commercial enablement.
Make sales, account management, customer success and onboarding fully ready to sell and support what we ship: positioning docs, discovery frameworks, competitive battlecards, demo narratives, objection handling, pricing and packaging talk tracks. Build the feedback loop from the field (Gong, win/loss, DC20, reference customers) back into the message, and use AI to make that loop continuous rather than quarterly: agents that mine calls for objections, generate first-draft battlecards from competitive signals, and keep enablement current as the product changes.

AI, explained to people who are tired of hearing about AI.
Dealers have been pitched "AI" for a decade. Our agents actually do the work. Own how we talk about AI to a pragmatic, ROI-driven buyer without hype, and give the company a point of view on the agentic future of dealership software that competitors have to respond to.

Voice of the buyer.
Sit with dealers, listen to sales calls, attend DC20, ride along with account managers. Product marketing here is written from the customer, not from other product marketers' decks.

The team and the discipline.
Lead and grow the product marketing team. Coach product managers on how to use product marketing as leverage: how to write a brief, how to think about positioning before the roadmap is locked, how to run a launch. Teach the company what good looks like, then systematize it.

An AI-native way of working.
Model it yourself and teach it to others. Build the agents, skills and workflows that let a small team operate like a large one: research synthesis, message testing, asset generation, enablement upkeep, competitive monitoring. Set the standard for how product marketers here use AI, coach your team and your PM partners to that standard, and be honest about where the tools fall short and human judgment has to do the work.

Cross-functional partnership.
Work as one team with Marketing (brand, demand and events), Sales, Customer Success and Product. In the near term you will also direct an outside agency engaged to add launch and content horsepower, with the explicit goal of bringing that capability in-house.

What success looks like

By 6 months:
the platform messaging architecture exists and is in use by sales and marketing; our launch system is defined, AI-assisted end to end, and has run at least two launches; the field says it is enabled on the current portfolio; your team is staffed and operating with clear ownership by pillar; NADA product marketing plan is locked.

By 12 months:
NADA launches executed to plan; the CRM-to-engagement-platform narrative is visible in analyst, press and customer language; enablement runs as a system rather than a scramble; product managers are producing better briefs and positioning because you taught them how; the product marketing team is visibly the most AI-fluent function in the company and other teams are borrowing its workflows; the agency dependency has been replaced with internal capability.

Who we are looking for

12+ years in B2B software marketing with deep product marketing roots, including 4+ years leading product marketers; you have built or rebuilt a product marketing function, not just inherited one.
You have taken a company through a single-product to multi-product or platform transition and owned the positioning work that came with it.
Player-coach by temperament. You can present to a CEO in the morning and write the battlecard yourself that afternoon, and you do not need a large team before you can be effective.
You bring patterns. You know what a good launch framework, messaging hierarchy, enablement program and competitive practice look like, and you can install a working version in your first quarter and improve it from there.
You have marketed AI, data or platform products to buyers who are not technologists, and you can talk credibly about how AI changes what the product is and how it should be positioned.
You are AI-native in how you work. You already use AI daily for research, drafting, analysis and asset production; you have built at least a few of your own agents, prompts or automations rather than only using what came in the box; and you have taught a team to work this way. You will be asked to show this, not describe it.
You write clearly and quickly. Strategy that cannot be written down is not strategy.
You have sold into both an SMB-style motion and a true enterprise motion, and you understand how the message changes across them.
Executive presence with low ego. Comfortable disagreeing with executives, comfortable being wrong in public, comfortable in a company that is humble, fast and consensus-leaning.
Experience in a PE- or growth-backed company where the plan is clear and the clock is real is a plus.

Nice to have:
automotive retail or dealer software experience, vertical SaaS, category creation or redefinition, pricing and packaging, analyst relations. If you do not know auto retail yet, we will teach you the industry; bring the judgment and the appetite to learn it fast.

Practicalities

YOUR MINDSET

You have developed fluency in disciplines most people keep separate. You don't see creative strategy, experience strategy and media strategy as different languages. You see them as different expressions of the same brilliant strategic thinking and that fluency informs everything you do.
You believe that the best creative ideas scale, that strategic coherence matters, and that you grow by collaborating with people who think differently than you. You contribute with conviction and follow-through. You help build a culture where people understand how their work fits into something bigger and you are here for more than your role. You understand that ideas and how they reach people are equally important—not one secondary to the other.

ROLE OVERVIEW

You will develop and execute a range of integrated strategy projects for one or two B2B brands. One of those brands is a multi-brand healthcare enterprise where you will translating strategic direction into inspirational insights and briefs that enable great creative, content and experience execution to come together.

This role demands fluency in two disciplines that most separate: Brand Strategy and Connections Strategy. You work from both perspectives simultaneously. You don't just translate between them,you hold them together with clear strategic thinking that helps them operate as one. You understand how strategy needs to live across earned, owned, and paid channels—including social and influencer partnerships and sales enablement.

You turn strategic direction into clear big ideas and briefs grounded in buying group insight and media possibility. You work with creative content, experience and media teams to help them understand how their work fits together into a coherent whole and inspire both to think bigger and think together. You are the bold strategic voice in the room who helps teams see how their work connects and why that connection matters.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Development — Ideas & Brief

Translate strategic direction into powerful Catalyzing Ideas and briefs grounded in creative insight and contextual possibility
Build the strategic rationale—not just what we're doing, but why it matters and how it moves the business
Develop brand worlds that breathe life into ideas—articulating character, conviction, and edges with specificity
Help creative teams uncover the strategic insight that should drive their work. Identify how ideas work across the full B2B lifecycle. Help media teams see how that idea scales. Understand how ideas need to live in social and influencer contexts
Develop content and sales enablement strategies that support the buying experience – going beyond the expected to elevate the brand a thought leader in the category while optimizing for LLMs

Strategic System Operationalization

Identify WHERE ideas reach the right buying groups and HOW they show up in context—across paid media, owned channels, social platforms, and influencer partnerships
Research and surface buyer signals that inform where and when strategy becomes relevant and urgent
Understand signal stacking—how multiple signals cluster to create moments of greatest impact
Help teams understand how their work feeds the whole and why that connection matters

Cross-Disciplinary Alignment & Leadership

Work with creative, content, media, social, and influencer partners to ensure strategy translates consistently across all touchpoints
Help creative teams understand the experience strategy and what's possible. Help media teams understand creative strategy and what ideas demand. Bridge social and influencer thinking into the broader strategic conversation.
Bridge creative and media conversations so both disciplines understand they're working from the same foundation
Think all languages simultaneously—you are fluent in creative strategy, experience strategy, content strategy AND media strategy, weaving them together

Stakeholder Communication & Relationship Building

Brief brand partners and internal stakeholders on strategy with clarity and confidence
Be a reliable strategic voice partners turn to when asking "how should this idea work?" or "how does this fit what we're doing?"
Engage with senior team to gather input and ensure alignment with enterprise priorities

Team Contribution & Development

Support team leadership by modeling integrated thinking
Mentor junior strategists, helping them understand systems thinking, not just tactical execution
Ask good questions that help teams think beyond their discipline
Contribute to creating psychological safety where people challenge siloed thinking

Measurement & Learning

Help monitor how strategy translates in market and gather feedback for refinement
Support measurement that tracks whether the system is working, using data as feedback not just reporting
Contribute insights on how ideas are propagating and whether signals are clustering as predicted

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Your strategic briefs are clear, actionable, and inspiring. You are a student of great work and hungry to do your best work
Creative, content and media partners use your strategy as a real tool, not just a document. They understand how the two disciplines work together
Teams understand the coherence in what they're building—how each piece connects to the whole. They think in systems, not just tactics
You've demonstrated you can develop strategy and help bring it to life in integrated ways
Junior strategists learn systems thinking by working with you. You are an inspiring mentor to junior talent
Measurement shows ideas propagating and signals clustering as predicted
Relationships deepen because you bring perspective that helps partners operate more strategically

KEY QUALIFICATIONS

Experience:

6-10 years strategy experience with demonstrated fluency in creative strategy, content strategy, experience strategy AND media strategy
Proven ability to develop and communicate breakthrough strategic thinking, not just execute briefs
Track record working on B2B brands in complex strategic environments
Experience working across creative, content, experience and media functions
Comfort engaging with senior stakeholders in strategic conversations
Experience with social media platforms and/or influencer partnerships a plus

Intellectual Foundation:

Understanding of how ideas propagate and land in culture—not just single-moment performance
Ability to hold multiple perspectives, audiences, and signals in mind simultaneously
Comfort moving between strategic thinking and tactical execution, between 30,000 feet and the work itself
Understanding of signal stacking—how audience signals cluster to create moments of greatest impact
Genuine curiosity about how creative and experience thinking complement and inform each other
Evidence that you think about systems, not just campaigns
Evidence that you learn from people and disciplines different from your own

Strong communicator who can brief stakeholders with clarity
Ability to contribute ideas within a broader strategic framework
Genuine interest in how creative and experience thinking complement each other
Collaborative spirit; you get smarter working with others
Ability to mentor and develop other strategists

About DriveCentric

Founded in 2010 and headquartered in St. Louis, MO, with a distributed team across the US.
Backed by Summit Partners, with a mandate to grow, not to trim.
Trusted by 3,300+ dealerships across the US and Canada, from single-store independents to multi-billion-dollar dealer groups, plus adjacent retail such as RV, marine and powersports.
Launched the Service Engagement Hub in August 2026, the first engagement platform built for fixed operations, and ships autonomous AI agents (Sales, Prospect, Nurture, Service-to-Sales, Performance Management, Service) on a monthly cadence.
One of the first automotive software companies certified to ISO/IEC 42001 for AI management.
Runs DC20, a dealer-led peer community and event series that most vendors would call a user conference and our customers call a 20 Group.

Why this role exists now

Three things are true at once:
The portfolio is multiplying. We are moving from one product line to a platform spanning sales, service, data, F&I, payments and digital retail. Each department has a different buyer, a different competitor set and a different vocabulary. Nobody owns the messaging architecture that ties them together.
Product velocity is ahead of field readiness. Engineering and product are shipping at a pace the company has never operated at. Sales, account management, onboarding and support need enablement that is timely, credible and actually used, and we do not yet have the system to produce it.
The category is up for grabs. The market wants to put us in the CRM box. Our thesis is that AI agents change what "CRM" means, and the company that explains that best to a skeptical, relationship-driven buyer wins the next decade of auto retail software. That story needs an owner.

And one thing underneath all three: we are building an AI-native company, not a company with an AI product. Engineering ships with AI, our internal agents answer the field's questions, and every function is expected to automate its own work. Product marketing has to be built that way from day one, which is why the person who builds it matters so much.

You will report to the Chief Product & Business Officer and sit on the product leadership team alongside the VP Product, the AI Labs lead and the Head of Product Operations. Two product marketing managers will report to you on day one, with room to grow the team as the pillars scale.

What you will own

Positioning and narrative.
Build and maintain the messaging architecture for the platform and each of its pillars: the umbrella story, the per-department stories, and the proof that connects them. Lead the multi-year narrative evolution from CRM to AI Engagement Platform, and make it land with three very different audiences: the owner-operator of one store, the centralized buying group running 5 to 15 rooftops, and the enterprise group with a CFO in the room.

Launches
. Design and run our new product introduction system: launch tiers, the artifacts each tier gets, who does what, and how we measure whether the launch worked. Build it AI-first, so that a monthly agent cadence produces a full set of launch assets without a monthly scramble. Then run the big ones yourself. NADA Show (February, Orlando) is the industry's Dreamforce and our largest launch moment of the year; you will own the product marketing plan for it.

Commercial enablement.
Make sales, account management, customer success and onboarding fully ready to sell and support what we ship: positioning docs, discovery frameworks, competitive battlecards, demo narratives, objection handling, pricing and packaging talk tracks. Build the feedback loop from the field (Gong, win/loss, DC20, reference customers) back into the message, and use AI to make that loop continuous rather than quarterly: agents that mine calls for objections, generate first-draft battlecards from competitive signals, and keep enablement current as the product changes.

AI, explained to people who are tired of hearing about AI.
Dealers have been pitched "AI" for a decade. Our agents actually do the work. Own how we talk about AI to a pragmatic, ROI-driven buyer without hype, and give the company a point of view on the agentic future of dealership software that competitors have to respond to.

Voice of the buyer.
Sit with dealers, listen to sales calls, attend DC20, ride along with account managers. Product marketing here is written from the customer, not from other product marketers' decks.

The team and the discipline.
Lead and grow the product marketing team. Coach product managers on how to use product marketing as leverage: how to write a brief, how to think about positioning before the roadmap is locked, how to run a launch. Teach the company what good looks like, then systematize it.

An AI-native way of working.
Model it yourself and teach it to others. Build the agents, skills and workflows that let a small team operate like a large one: research synthesis, message testing, asset generation, enablement upkeep, competitive monitoring. Set the standard for how product marketers here use AI, coach your team and your PM partners to that standard, and be honest about where the tools fall short and human judgment has to do the work.

Cross-functional partnership.
Work as one team with Marketing (brand, demand and events), Sales, Customer Success and Product. In the near term you will also direct an outside agency engaged to add launch and content horsepower, with the explicit goal of bringing that capability in-house.

What success looks like

By 6 months:
the platform messaging architecture exists and is in use by sales and marketing; our launch system is defined, AI-assisted end to end, and has run at least two launches; the field says it is enabled on the current portfolio; your team is staffed and operating with clear ownership by pillar; NADA product marketing plan is locked.

By 12 months:
NADA launches executed to plan; the CRM-to-engagement-platform narrative is visible in analyst, press and customer language; enablement runs as a system rather than a scramble; product managers are producing better briefs and positioning because you taught them how; the product marketing team is visibly the most AI-fluent function in the company and other teams are borrowing its workflows; the agency dependency has been replaced with internal capability.

Who we are looking for

12+ years in B2B software marketing with deep product marketing roots, including 4+ years leading product marketers; you have built or rebuilt a product marketing function, not just inherited one.
You have taken a company through a single-product to multi-product or platform transition and owned the positioning work that came with it.
Player-coach by temperament. You can present to a CEO in the morning and write the battlecard yourself that afternoon, and you do not need a large team before you can be effective.
You bring patterns. You know what a good launch framework, messaging hierarchy, enablement program and competitive practice look like, and you can install a working version in your first quarter and improve it from there.
You have marketed AI, data or platform products to buyers who are not technologists, and you can talk credibly about how AI changes what the product is and how it should be positioned.
You are AI-native in how you work. You already use AI daily for research, drafting, analysis and asset production; you have built at least a few of your own agents, prompts or automations rather than only using what came in the box; and you have taught a team to work this way. You will be asked to show this, not describe it.
You write clearly and quickly. Strategy that cannot be written down is not strategy.
You have sold into both an SMB-style motion and a true enterprise motion, and you understand how the message changes across them.
Executive presence with low ego. Comfortable disagreeing with executives, comfortable being wrong in public, comfortable in a company that is humble, fast and consensus-leaning.

Nice to have:

Practicalities
